errata.reason: The assembled problem gives the hypotenuse and one leg, sets |BC|=a and requires A to be on the perpendicular through C with |AB| equal to the given hypotenuse. The existence condition in p0139#10 is c>a. Thus the locus of A about center B has radius c=|AB|, not the point C. Replacing only capital C by lowercase c yields (B,c), consistent with the given data and the subsequent existence condition. This is an author proposal, not registered or approved errata. The preceding disclaimer is historical: these exact spans were subsequently approved by the independent source-bound review, approval SHA256 cc2e3c763aa6c8f253325d5b5dca1445b2db7a9383fefda6ea69a127a07fa1cf.

Step 1 constructs BC=a and step 2 constructs the perpendicular through C. To enforce the other given datum |AB|=c, step 3 must draw the circle centered at B with radius c. A capital C labels the right-angle vertex, not the prescribed length. If it instead meant BC=a, that circle would meet the perpendicular only at C and give a degenerate triangle. Only the radius letter changes; all faithful wording and punctuation remain. This is an author proposal, not registered or approved errata.
